A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AIDD, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references and has no appendices; v3 includes readable Supplementary Material A–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original MusicNet inpainting results using FAD, LSD, and ODG in Section 6, Table 1, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original MusicNet and MAESTRO evaluations and training-component ablations in Sections 6–7 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: v3 retains the WavTokenizer–DiT backbone but extends DWDSE training with an embedding-derivative regularization loss and noise-dependent geometric span masking (Sections 4.2–4.3). These introduce substantive changes to the training objective and corruption procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds MAESTRO piano inpainting with 375 and 750 ms gaps. MusicNet reporting shifts from short-gap evaluations including 50 and 100 ms to 150–300 ms. v1's abstract mentions MTG evaluation through 500 ms without corresponding experimental details or results; that assertion disappears.

E2.justification: The MusicNet comparison retains LPC, A-SPAIN-L, CQT-Diff+, and the masked reference from v1 Figure 3. v3 Table 2 adds an evaluated comparator group comprising GACELA, bin2bin, and bin2bin-MIDI on MAESTRO; these were not evaluated against AIDD in v1.

E3.justification: v3 retains MusicNet's 60-segment, four-gap design and the base model's 400,000-step training, but specifies 100,000 steps for new variants. MAESTRO introduces 150,000-step training, six-second evaluation clips with one central gap, and PEA-Q evaluation. The reported inference crossfade changes from 10 to 6 ms.

E4.justification: v3 introduces a dedicated ablation study comparing the DWDSE base, span masking, derivative regularization, and their combination. Table 3 also tests regularization weights, derivative order, and span-distribution parameters at 200 and 300 ms. v1 contains no comparable component or hyperparameter analysis.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages without uncertainty estimates. v3 first specifies averaging ten stochastic generations per MusicNet segment and adds ± values in Tables 2–3. It does not define those uncertainty terms or report independent training-seed counts, so this establishes expanded reporting rather than an increase in training runs.

E6.justification: Even the retained DWDSE base has revised MusicNet results: FAD at 200/300 ms changes from 3.0489/3.8067 in v1 Table 1 to 2.802/4.015 in v3 Table 3. Reported protocol differences prevent a clean same-setting performance comparison. v3 also adds variant results and MAESTRO PEA-Q ODG scores of -2.370 and -2.959 at 375/750 ms.

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical definitions for first- and second-order embedding derivatives, their masked-position regularization loss, and the combined objective. It also formalizes a noise-dependent span-length distribution and masking budget (Sections 4.2–4.3). These substantially extend the mathematical formulation beyond v1's diffusion background; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The contribution expands from applying discrete diffusion to audio inpainting to introducing two training innovations. The abstract and conclusion now claim performance on MusicNet and MAESTRO through 750 ms, replacing v1's MusicNet results and asserted MTG/500 ms coverage. The abstract also strengthens the performance claim to consistent outperformance for gaps of 150 ms and above.

C2.justification: v3 adds mechanism explanations connecting derivative regularization to temporal continuity and span masking to structured corruption. It interprets subset-trained MAESTRO results as resource-efficient generalization, acknowledges CQT-Diff+'s 150 ms FAD advantage, and explicitly discusses speech and language-model extensions as future work. These extend v1's general token-space coherence argument.

D1.justification: v3 adds selected regularization and span hyperparameters, MATLAB PEA-Q implementation information, MAESTRO subset-selection notes, and code-submission/future-release statements in Supplementary Material A–E. Optimizer, batch size, token length, and hardware were already documented in v1. Exact MAESTRO subset sizes and membership remain unspecified, and the PDFs do not provide the stated code.

R1.justification: v3 adds the two Aironi works and references supporting MAESTRO, PEA-Q, and LPC, while removing Anderson and Campbell. It explicitly positions the new training components as extensions of Lou et al. The broader survey and continuous-versus-discrete framing remain substantially the same.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the introduction gains an explicit contribution list, and related work is substantially condensed. v3 removes the standalone tokenizer background, consolidates architecture subsections, and moves inference and evaluation descriptions into the experimental setup. These constitute extensive rewriting and reorganization of existing material.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the separate training and inference diagrams with a redesigned combined Figure 1. MusicNet comparisons move from v1's three-panel Figure 3 and AIDD-only table to a multi-method table. New MAESTRO, ablation, and hyperparameter tables further change the presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the empirical support for the central long-gap argument: v1's MTG/500 ms assertion lacked corresponding results, whereas v3 provides explicit MAESTRO comparisons through 750 ms. Table 3 also makes the added training components assessable through component and sensitivity comparisons. Unspecified MAESTRO subsets, undefined uncertainty terms, unequal base/variant training budgets, and an overstated claim of combined-method superiority limit confidence. Nevertheless, the new checkable evidence and clearer experimental account provide a substantial net improvement.
